review_notes: POB-vb-1wora-001 closes INV-CODEC-TB-003 (cheap-before-expensive ordering) and INV-CODEC-TB-006 (diagnostic code wiring parity) via structural review. The command is concrete (grep + diff against HEAD for both decode sites and the diagnostic_code()/symbolic_code() match arms) and the expected_evidence specifies the exact post-fix shape. No executable verifier can express call-ordering as cheaply. Required lanes are correctly identified; no waivers. Accepted.

POB-vb-1wora-003 covers INV-CODEC-TB-002 (Ok only if bytes.len() == payload_end) and the round-trip preservation claim via property-based random JournalEvent round-trip. Proptest is the cheapest verifier for this universal claim; the 1024-case budget is standard. Mutual exclusion with UnexpectedEof is locked via the proptest_decode_record_payload_mutual_exclusion_with_unexpected_eof property (covered in POB-vb-1wora-005). Required; accepted.

POB-vb-1wora-004 extends the existing kani_postcard_envelope_wire.rs file (H1-H5 already present; H5 at line 277 uses #[kani::unwind(4)] for the same header shape) with kani_harness_rejects_trailing_bytes (H6) that stubs verify_digest_match as a counted call and asserts the count is 0 for any input where bytes.len() > payload_end. Bounds are concrete: 60-byte header, payload_len bounded by MAX_JOURNAL_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES, trailing bytes in 1..=8, #[kani::unwind(4)] inherited from H5. This is the only verifier that mechanically proves call-ordering rather than relying on review. Required; accepted.

POB-vb-1wora-007 extends fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_storage_codec_payload_corruption.rs (existing target, libFuzzer wrapper) with fuzz_target_trailing_bytes. The oracle is concrete: build a valid record, append N (0..=8) random trailing bytes, assert Err(TrailingBytes { trailing: N }) when N > 0 and Ok when N == 0. The 60-second wallclock budget is the AGENTS.md fuzz discipline. The existing fuzz crate is at fuzz/fuzz_targets/ with libFuzzer harness patterns already in place. Fallback per A-005 is documented: blocked_tooling if cargo +nightly fuzz is unavailable, with POB-002 directed tests still covering the invariant. Required; accepted.

not_applicable is correct. decode_record_payload and decode_envelope_only are pure parsers over &[u8] with no concurrent memory ordering, no Send/Sync shared-state, no Arc/Mutex/atomic in body or callees (verify_digest_match, decode_record_header). The vb_storage crate has #![forbid(unsafe_code)] and the codec/* modules contain no std::sync imports. Limitation_kind='single-threaded-pure-parser' is concrete. Three evidence refs back the decision (codec/payload.rs:56-82, codec/envelope.rs:48-83, contracts/hazard-analysis.md §2.5). Loom would not expose new bugs beyond what Kani H6 already proves about byte-level inputs. Accepted.

not_applicable is correct. vb_storage has #![forbid(unsafe_code)] workspace-wide; the post-fix trailing-bytes check is a pure usize compare + subtraction (if bytes.len() > payload_end { return Err(JournalError::TrailingBytes { trailing: bytes.len() - payload_end }); }) with no raw pointers, no MaybeUninit, no aliasing. The new TrailingBytes { trailing: usize } variant contains only a usize field. Miri would find no UB paths. Limitation_kind='forbid-unsafe-crate' is concrete. Three evidence refs back the decision (vb_storage crate header, the post-fix check shape, contracts/hazard-analysis.md §2.6). Accepted.

not_applicable is correct. The fix introduces no refinement type, no indexed type, no constraint refinement. The trailing > 0 invariant is enforced structurally at the producer site (bytes.len() > payload_end mathematically implies trailing = bytes.len() - payload_end > 0), not by a refinement annotation. The error variant is a plain enum with a usize field. The Verus mirror handles the refinement claim at the bridge level (POB-vb-1wora-006 via the trailing == (bytes.len() as u32) - expected_payload_end && trailing > 0 precondition). Limitation_kind='no-refinement-types-introduced' is concrete. Four evidence refs back the decision. Accepted.

Four evidence refs back the decision (proof-planner skill doctrine, decode_record_payload purity, contracts/hazard-analysis.md §2.1, no state-machine introduction). Accepted.
